data.one_liner: Flutter plugin that sends uncaught errors and crash reports to Firebase Crashlytics.
data.what_it_does: Integrates Firebase Crashlytics into a Flutter app, automatically capturing uncaught exceptions and custom logs. It uploads crash symbols for Android and iOS to improve stack traces in the Firebase console.
use_when: You need automatic crash reporting for Flutter apps
You already use other Firebase services and want a unified backend
avoid_when: You cannot modify native Android/iOS projects (e.g., pure web Flutter)
You need a lightweight, pure‑Dart solution without native SDKs
strengths: Handles symbol upload and native crash data
Supported on Android, iOS, and macOS
weaknesses: Requires native setup and platform-specific configuration
Minimum Android SDK 24 and macOS 11 may limit older devices
data.setup_notes: Add Firebase configuration files (GoogleService-Info.plist, google-services.json), update Android build.gradle and iOS podfile, ensure firebase_core is initialized, and set up Crashlytics in native projects.

alternatives.name: firebase_core
alternatives.why_pick_it: Required for any Firebase plugin; provides core initialization

alternatives.name: firebase_analytics
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need analytics without crash reporting

alternatives.name: firebase_remote_config
alternatives.why_pick_it: For remote feature flags when crash reporting isn’t needed
